title: Fix 'is not a git command' by finding the right git subcommand
summary: Git prints "is not a git command" when the word after git is misspelled or does not exist. Git suggests the closest real command, and you can list all of them to find the right one.

aliases.text: git is not a git command

error_patterns: is not a git command. See 'git --help'.

steps.explain: List every command git knows. Look for the real name closest to the word git rejected. The list is grouped under headings such as 'Main Porcelain Commands'; each line is a command name followed by a short description.
steps.expect: A long list of command names, for example 'status' with 'Show the working tree status'.

steps.explain: Narrow the list to lines that contain part of the name you are looking for. Replace <PART> with a few letters you remember, such as stat.

placeholders.name: PART
placeholders.description: Part of the git command name you are looking for

steps.expect: One or more lines with the real command name, such as 'status' followed by its description.

steps.explain: Run git again with the correct command name in place of the misspelled one. git status shows the state of your project; it works only inside a folder that is a git repository (made with git init or git clone).
steps.expect: Inside a repository: a line 'On branch ...' and a list of changed files. Outside a repository: 'fatal: not a git repository'.

verify.expect: A line that starts with 'status' and says 'Show the working tree status'.

source.title: git manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
